model_output.verdict: A product designer with named deliverables, but little about the decisions or results behind them.
write_up: You designed apps at Loop Fitness and sites and app screens at Brightpath Studio, and you're now a barista at Ferry Street Coffee. It's common for design resumes to list deliverables without explaining the decisions behind them. Here, that makes it harder to stand out for product design work because a recruiter can't see what the designs solved.

The Figma design system is the best model: it names what you created, where you built it, and why it was a first for the app. Your current job accounts for the time since Loop Fitness, but your resume doesn't show product design work after that role.

Let's start with the Loop Fitness booking flow and weekly releases. Add the problem you worked on and your contribution, then use the usability tests to show what you did with the findings. Your portfolio link gives you another place to show that work.

cards.line: - Prepare drinks and serve customers in a busy cafe
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the job, but not how many customers you serve or drinks you prepare. A measure of the work would give the current role more substance.
cards.example: Prepare drinks and serve [number] customers [time period] in a busy cafe
cards.question: How many customers do you serve in a typical shift?

cards.line: - Train new baristas on espresso equipment
cards.cannot_tell: Training new baristas is useful to know. How many have you trained, and what does the training cover?
cards.example: Train [number] new baristas on espresso equipment, covering [what training includes]
cards.question: How many new baristas have you trained, and what do you teach them?

cards.line: - Designed the class booking flow for the iOS and Android apps
cards.cannot_tell: The booking flow is a clear piece of work, but the problem behind it is missing. That makes it tough to see how you approached the design.
cards.example: Designed the class booking flow for the iOS and Android apps to address [booking problem]
cards.question: What booking problem did the flow address?

cards.line: - Worked with two engineers and a product manager on weekly releases
cards.cannot_tell: The team and release rhythm are clear, but your contribution to those releases isn't. What design work did you bring to them?
cards.example: Worked with two engineers and a product manager on weekly releases, contributing [your design work]
cards.question: What design work did you contribute to the weekly releases?

cards.line: - Created the app's first design system in Figma
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives you ownership of a distinct piece of work rather than leaving a recruiter to guess what you contributed.

cards.line: - Ran usability tests with members before launches
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter knows who took part and when you tested, but not what you did with what you learned. That connection matters for a product design role.
cards.example: Ran usability tests with members before launches and [what you did with the findings]
cards.question: What did you do with the findings from those tests?

fit.note: Your design work points toward product design roles involving apps and web experiences. The most recent product design role ended in February 2024, so showing the thinking behind that work will be important.
